- [2023/05/23] William Blake's poetry is characterized by themes of tension between material and spiritual worlds, transformative power of imagination, and pervasive Christian symbolism.
- [2023/05/23] Blake's work was not well-received during his lifetime due to its unconventional style and critical stance towards societal norms and the Church.
- [2023/05/23] William Butler Yeats was deeply influenced by Blake's mystical and symbolic vision, incorporating similar themes in his poetry.
- [2023/05/23] T.S. Eliot referenced Blake's work in poems such as "The Waste Land," showing the influence of Blake on modernist literature.
- [2023/05/23] Allen Ginsberg was inspired by Blake's radical individualism and use of prophetic voice, reflecting this influence in his Beat Generation poetry.
- [2023/05/23] Walt Whitman admired Blake's work, sharing themes of individualism, mysticism, and the power of imagination with Blake.
- [2023/05/23] Dante Gabriel Rossetti was inspired by Blake's use of symbolism and exploration of spiritual themes in his Pre-Raphaelite art.
- [2023/05/23] William Morris was influenced by Blake's emphasis on individual creativity and critique of industrialization, impacting his design work.
- [2023/05/23] Max Ernst found inspiration in Blake's unconventional imagery and exploration of the subconscious mind for surrealist art.
